decision_context: D-HIST-03-1 = C (José): take fa16, ta21, ta22 from AddBiomechanics one participant at a time; make sure the metadata columns can be reconstructed.
method: Official AddBiomechanics Drive tree listed (HTML folder pages only) for the six No_Arm folders of the three studies: 36 B3D files, the same 36 members as the archive central directory (sha256 88d494cc...).

Headers only: for 15 members (all 11 fa16, ta21 s3 and s8, ta22 04 and 10) bytes 0-7 and then the header range were requested from the uncompressed Drive copy (single-range 206). Frame bytes were never requested. Total transferred 92,051,439 bytes.
Headers parsed with a minimal protobuf wire decoder against SubjectOnDisk.proto (nimblephysics c405b056); absent proto3 fields are reported as absent, not as enum defaults.

Publications: Falisse 2017 accepted manuscript text (pypdf), Tan 2022 abstract (PubMed E-utilities), Tan 2023 abstract (Semantic Scholar), the Tan README, and one secondary article that describes the Tan 2023 dataset protocol.

header_layout.note: Tan headers are 8.8-19.9 MB because per-frame quality arrays (missing-GRF reason, marker RMS, residuals) are in the header.

falisse_attribution.finding: Exactly one of the 35 four-man/four-woman subsets of the 11 AddBiomechanics Falisse subjects reproduces all six cohort statistics the TBME 2017 paper reports: subject_0, subject_2, subject_3, subject_4, subject_5, subject_6, subject_9, subject_10. The folder is very likely the paper's 8 volunteers plus 3 additional men (subject_1 (43 y), subject_7 (37 y), subject_8 (39 y)).

subset_test.rounding: age and mass mean and SD to 0.1, height mean to 1 cm and SD to 0.1 cm, as reported
subset_test.earlier_error: The first HIST-04 version read ages outside 29.8 ± 3.9 as a contradiction; a mean ± SD is not a range. Corrected after independent verification (HIST-04-verify.json).

falisse_attribution.paper: 8 volunteers (4 male, 4 female), age 29.8 ± 3.9 y, height 176 ± 6.6 cm, mass 69.6 ± 6.0 kg; 11 datasets = 11 legs (7 left, 4 right); six motions: gait, squat, stair descent, stair ascent, sit-to-stand-to-sit, squat jump.
falisse_attribution.addbiomechanics: 11 subjects with 11 distinct sex/age/height/mass records (7 male, 4 female), age range 24-43 y; trials only Gait, STS and StairUp.
unresolved: Who the 3 extra men are and which study they come from.

The trials: the files hold 3 of the paper's 6 motions (gait, sit-to-stand, stair ascent as Gait/STS/StairUp); squat, stair descent and squat jump are absent. Why, and whether these trials follow the paper's protocol, is not stated.
falisse_attribution.consequence: Demographics for all 11 come from the headers either way. The paper's citation is likely right for 8 subjects, but its protocol facts (motions, overground plates, 100 Hz, legs) and the task mapping are not applied until the source of the 3 extra subjects and of the trials is confirmed. Falisse is not releasable until then; acquisition is not blocked.
falisse_attribution.needed: Yes/no for José (outward-facing): ask the AddBiomechanics team or the KU Leuven authors (a) whether subjects 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 are the TBME volunteers, (b) who subjects 1, 7 and 8 are, and (c) which protocol the Gait/STS/StairUp trials came from.

mass_check.finding: The dynamics pass carries its own mass-tuned model whose total body mass differs from the entered subject mass.
mass_check.consequence: Moments from the dynamics pass are consistent with the tuned model, not the entered mass (fa16 ratio 0.71x to 1.80x; subject_1: 118.0 kg tuned versus 65.5 kg entered). Normalization mass is a conversion convention for José in the canonical-mapping step; both masses are reconstructable from the header. Not checked: whether total model mass is what AddBiomechanics used for each frame's inverse dynamics.
mass_check.source: model_osim_text <mass> elements per pass in the B3D header; nimblephysics docs: the dynamics pass 'further solves for the mass distribution' (https://nimblephysics.org/docs/working-with-addbiomechanics-data.html)

processing_pass.found: Every trial read has passes in the order kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics (index 0, 1, 2). The lowPassFilter pass records a 30 Hz, order-2 Butterworth. Filter fields in the kinematics and dynamics pass headers hold uninitialized-looking values and are ignored.
processing_pass.legacy: Legacy LocoHub converters read processingPasses[1], which is the lowPassFilter pass in all 15 headers read (HIST-03 found the same in Tiziana2019 Subject29).
processing_pass.proposal: Convert the dynamics pass: per the nimblephysics docs it 'takes as input the previous pass outputs ... and then further solves for the mass distribution, fine tunes bone scales, and tunes motion of the skeleton that best matches the experimental force data'. Its values will differ from the legacy files. Pass choice is part of D-HIST-04-1.

row_design.current_adapter: convert_addbiomechanics_to_parquet.py writes 1 raw-sensor row + 1 row per pass per frame as JSON payloads (4 rows per frame here).
row_design.proposal: One row per frame from one pass (dynamics), numeric columns, both legs as two reference_side identities of the same rows' recording, flagged frames kept with their missing_GRF_reason (never deleted silently).
lost_in_proposal: raw marker trajectories and raw per-plate force/CoP/torque readings
root-frame copies, joint centres, spatial velocity/acceleration histories
per-frame marker RMS and residual arrays (they stay in the pinned B3D)
row_design.recoverable: Only by re-fetching: the plan deletes each B3D after conversion, so left-out passes, raw markers and raw plate readings can be recovered only by downloading the member again from the archive while it still serves the same bytes (checked against archive ETag, central-directory CRC32 and the SHA-256 recorded at acquisition) and reconverting. If the archive changes or disappears, they are lost to LocoHub.

estimate.basis: Frames exact for the 15 headers read, estimated for the other 21 members. Every trial read has 3 passes. Bytes are float64 values before Parquet compression for the listed signals; compressed sizes are not measured. Option C stores every frame field as JSON text (the B3D frame data alone is about 29.6 GB in binary).

acquisition_plan.route: Archive zip member by HTTP range from archive.simtk.org (stable ETag, CRC32 in the central directory); inflate while streaming to one B3D file; the Drive copy is used only as a cross-check of the header hash.
acquisition_plan.why_not_drive: Drive publishes no checksum, may throttle (untested) and transfers 1.35x more bytes (uncompressed).
acquisition_plan.transient_disk: One expanded B3D at a time. Largest 2,215,534,429 bytes (ta21 s3); 6 of 8 ta21 files exceed 2.0 GB, so the 'under 2 GB' stated in D-HIST-03-1 does not hold: HIST-03 quoted the compressed size (1.64 GB), but the reader needs the expanded file. Peak is 2.22 GB; disk free about 153 GiB. Logged as an agent resource decision; staying under 2 GB would need a streaming frame decoder instead of the nimblephysics reader.
script_requirements: New contributor_tools/acquire_addbiomechanics_member.py (not written; specs bind a placeholder hash).
Refuse to start if any *.b3d exists anywhere under the HIST-04 destination (one transient B3D at a time).
HEAD the archive; refuse on an ETag or Content-Length change. Read the 30-byte local header at the bound offset; refuse unless name, method 8 and sizes match the central directory.

Stream the compressed payload with a 1 MiB buffer and a 2 MiB/s ceiling, inflate (raw deflate) straight to <subject>.b3d.partial; compute SHA-256 of the compressed and expanded streams and CRC32 of the expanded stream; refuse on CRC32 or size mismatch.

Check the expanded header: int64 length then header bytes; when a Drive header hash is bound, the header SHA-256 must equal it. Check the layout arithmetic (8 + header + frames x (sensor + passes x pass frame) = file size).

fsync, publish with a no-clobber rename, write acquisition_result.json (hashes, HTTP headers, header summary, status, scientific_approval false). Preserve partial files on failure; stop on a STOP file.
RLIMIT_AS 256 MiB; disk reserve and Windows free memory checked every 15 s.
The B3D is deleted only by the later conversion job after its outputs verify; the next acquisition refuses while it exists.
acquisition_plan.order: fa16 by size (pilot: subject_1, smallest), then ta22 by size, then ta21 by size; one job per tool call, each after a fresh admission. The first job is the pilot; a later study starts only after the previous study's first conversion is reviewed.

forbidden_inventions: ta21 speed from the tokens 24/28 (unit unstated; 2.4/2.8 m/s would be a guess).
ta21 strike pattern from SR/SI/baseline, or 'minimalist' from 'mini'.
ta22 speed or modification level per segment, or applying the cohort mean self-selected speed to a participant.
fa16 protocol facts (overground, 100 Hz, motions, legs) from the TBME paper while the trials and the 3 extra subjects are unexplained.
Rounding fa16 timesteps (100.1-100.5 Hz) to 100 Hz.
Reading absent trial_type/data_quality fields as their enum defaults (treadmill/pilotData).
Treating consecutive segments as one continuous recording or offsetting time by split_index.
not_checked: Frame bytes of any file (headers only); 21 of 36 headers not read (their frames are estimated).
Whether the lowPassFilter pass carries joint moments or GRF equal to the dynamics pass.
The Tan 2022 and Tan 2023 full texts (institutional access); the SimTK imukinetics HDF5 for condition labels.
Participant crosswalks to the papers; Falisse source study.
nimblephysics availability in the conversion environment; conversion throughput and compressed output size.
